title: The Figure Over the Wool

arc.title: The Cold Stone
arc.subtitle: a warm stone, already going cold

epigraph.text: The slate is read over what the wool covers, and the wool gives back no figure. A bell is four, four and a gap, and the gap has no payer until somebody puts a name under it.
epigraph.attribution: Two sayings of the Clay Yard, told at the first market of the second firing

pov: Daniel Marchetti (Corin), close third-person past tense inside a body of two hundred and forty-nine to two hundred and fifty-one days, six months and sixty-nine days to six months and seventy-one days, carried everywhere in a basket and told by nobody. The surgeon's register colours the noticing --- the file turned out as instruments on a towel and found exact, complete and worth nothing at two inches of air; the body inventoried as a wound is inventoried, crust, gap, frozen thread, cold and afterdrop in the order they arrive; the first reading of Smoke opened as a wound is opened, a figure passing over a covered thing and leaving the cost under the wool where no signature stands; the bell's four, four and a gap kept beside the told bell and not counted as a seventh hearing; the figure read over the basket held apart from the figure paid, with the first arithmetic of Smoke gone up the clay road in a locked box and answering nothing for the man carried out on Day 188 or the hand that went in on Seed 15 --- without a present-tense Chicago break or a tagged remembered line; the old life stays offstage and there is no departure from his eyes, no Court, collector, Waiting Room or back-room interior, no hearing beyond six, no seventh of the full note, no tenth stopping before the seventh year at its very end and still ungiven, no sixth asking and no witness for the row question, no sixth shape of the record-first hand, no eighth green or eighth shape, no name spoken over either, no sale, no calling of the loan, no naming of a payer, no private record opened, read or copied, no figure given for the dressed grain or for the hand that did not come back, no lesson made of the one opening before Smoke 1 which is behind the household and not looked at again, and no ending.

scenes.title: The Morning Earned
scenes.synopsis: First of six entries, first dated heading and the chapter's only drop cap (\dropcap on the opening words): Day 249, Smoke 10, Tenthday, small hours under the Vail kiln-house roof, then before first grey and into the morning at the hearth and the kiln mouth. Open in the small hours with the hand laid down against the fold on the seventy-second answer and the file open on the towel; set that coordination down like a tool, never recalled as a sign, growth, reaching, gift or power. Count carried at 248 exact, six months and sixty-eight days, told by nobody, coming into **249**, six months and sixty-nine days (T071/T072); the carried fire's fifth unpaid two hundred and forty-nine days, its payer unnamed (T088). First smell hot clay under tallow, wet wool under that, sour Ash breath of the unswept corner the house calls the thaw; first sound the kiln drawing in fours with a gap, not a bell --- Smoke 10 is that morning's work and the market is not brought into the small hours. Three counts in three places --- the kiln's four low pulls and the silence where the fifth should stand under the floor, the river's note of water over water through the finger's-width door, the boards' four nails, four and a thumb-width knot --- none rising into another, for agreeing them would want a payer and none stands to any (T061/T082). Body inventory: one stiff leathery brown-edged barley crust two inches from the ear, its empty place unnamed and no third; thread frozen and unwiped; cold stopped at cheek, temple and the bare wrist-joint where the wool rides back; the afterdrop waiting past a warming nobody in this house will perform; the surgeon takes the inventory and enters it nowhere (T060/T086). Sella goes to the fire before the basket, tells it the thaw, turns the coals with the back of a broken pot, says *The house will keep it*, counts under her breath toward no opening, pushes coal-black hair back with the burn-wrist so the grey streak shows pale; the widow's mark hangs where it hangs, untouched at shelf, well, rack, road and basket, the one opening before Smoke 1 behind the household, not looked at again (T058/T079). The dressed grain is turned under wool for damp, spread thin, gathered back by the handful and the fold set flat; changed state, gained no figure, entered on no slate, laid across no absence, the figure a reading will later speak over it not knowing what it cost (T077). A neighbour's cost-question goes to the pot and the weather with nothing priced; a man come down the clay road with dried pale mud-scurf brings a number up out of a fist toward the well, looks at it and puts it back into his sleeve, so the figure arrives nowhere and is not a missing figure (T015/T041/T047 held). Garl is kept in objects, name unspoken two hundred and forty-nine days, no collector up or down the clay road (T009/T013/T092). First hand question: the hand outside the wool goes up an inch toward the low note through the finger's-width door and comes down at once on the river's next low note; answer **seventy-three** filed on the sixth place with no payer named, not a longer reach, miss entered as a finding, hearing, seventh, tenth stopping, payment, held change, key, power or rule (T061/T082). At the going of the light Sella lifts the basket to carry him down to the Cross, giving every instruction to the wool and the wind and none to the basket.

scenes.title: The First Reading of Smoke
scenes.synopsis: Second entry of Day 249, no new dated heading: the first Account-day and market of the second firing, morning into afternoon at the Cross, the reading block under the moot-post, the pot board, the north bridge and the clay road, then home at the going of the light. **The chapter's one meaningful change** (T015/T041/T047, T077 advanced, not paid): Smoke's first reading gathers every withholding in one square and reads none of them. Sella sets the basket in the moot-post's finger's width of shade where no slate lies and stands half a pace off, giving no instruction and no reason to the basket. Eight pigs go over the wet boards and two hundred lean in. Berr Clay comes up short off the clay road with the red wool cord of his office folded square under his coat and the green of tasted lead glaze at one mouth-corner, hot clay under the smell of nothing at all; his large clean hands wipe the thumb twice before touching nothing, once for the slate and once for the figure that will be on it, hold a narrow slate unopened to the forearm, pass a finger over the figure and let the eyes rest on the writing a breath longer than the writing required, read *one in twelve, as the notice says* low into the crowd, the figure going twice over the basket, once for the moot and once for the households that came late; he calls the levy, denies it with *your house*, never *I*, and goes off toward High Kiln with the box locked and the true subtraction inside, believing he has done a kindness. The district's arithmetic changes for the first time in Smoke and cannot be undone; the printed figure stands unchallenged, the figure read aloud is still not the figure paid, it answers nothing for the man carried out on Day 188 or the hand that went in on Seed 15, and the space between the figure read over the covered grain at home and what that grain cost has no signature. The bell goes four, four and a gap with nobody crossing himself, the heard bell kept beside the told bell (T078). Hessa Rale goes up the clay road toward Greybank before noon with Berr's narrow slate held edge-on to her forearm and the writing turned to her sleeve, her hand arriving before her eyes arrive at the crowd; to a woman who asks what she carries she answers the question put and not the one behind it with *I don't read it. I carry it. There's a difference, and the road doesn't care which* and *Cross to Greybank. Reading goes up before noon. I've got a road to walk*; no figure comes off the slate, her order of reaching stays the eighth record-first hand on a place of its own, advanced and not paid (T080). Below the north bridge the soft-cuffed clerk stays set at the out-of-line landing for a measure nobody called, hand to slate before eyes to stalls (T090). The green-mouthed woman at the pot board and the foundling at the market's edge are deliberately offstage: no eighth green and no eighth shape, no name, no loaf, no slate, no sale, no joining (T050/T051, T033/T034 held). Second hand question: the hand goes up an inch toward the bell, is held through the gap where the next stroke did not come, and comes down on the next sound in the square --- an interval held against the absence of a stroke, filed as answer **seventy-four**, not a hearing, not a seventh of the full note, not a power (T061/T082). At the going of the light Sella carries him home at the half-pace from every open slate, goes wide around the clean dark line and the thaw, the rack space, the pan's gone ring, the bare trough, the field's empty place and the returning-line place, each with a look and no number, and says nothing of what was read over him (T098, T009/T013/T092).

scenes.title: The Arithmetic Behind
scenes.synopsis: Third entry, third dated heading: Day 250, Smoke 11, Firstday, small hours under the Vail roof, then the ordinary morning at the hearth, the loaf shelf, the drying racks and the yard well. New day, new date, no recap: **250** exact, six months and seventy days, nobody told; the carried fire's fifth unpaid two hundred and fifty days (T088); Smoke's first arithmetic gone up the clay road in Berr's locked box and unread under this roof, the figure read over the basket still not the figure paid; widow's mark touched once before the kiln on Smoke 1 and at no shelf, well, rack, road, basket, afternoon or dusk (T058/T079). First smell hot clay under tallow, wet wool under that, sour Ash breath of the thaw; first sound the kiln in fours with its gap, no bell, no market and no Cross; Smoke 20 (Day 259), the second Account-day, stands eight mornings beyond the close and is unbrought. The dressed grain is turned under wool for damp, spread thin, gathered back by the handful and the fold set flat; changed state, gained no figure, entered on no slate, laid across no absence (T077). A neighbour's cost-question goes to the pot and the weather; a man come down the clay road with a number in his fist brings it up toward the well, looks at it and puts it back into his sleeve, so the figure arrives nowhere (T015/T041/T047 held). Sella lips along the two-gapped row without a figure, glances once at the clay jar cold under its glaze and shuts her hand half over nothing, keeps her finger on top of the shelf's front edge so the charcoal tally stays unread and uncounted, sets the pot rim out and turns its handle two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat at the setting and no look toward the bed (T100). The yard goes around the clean dark line and the new finer grey called the thaw, the space beneath the lowest rack with its broken birth-slates, the round ring where the shallow clay pan stood, the bare dark trough, the field's empty place out on the worked strips and the returning-line place where a hand went in on Seed 15 and did not come back, each with a look and a wide step and no number (T098 carried, T060/T086, T009/T013/T092). **Ilva sighting, T080 held at nine and not advanced to a tenth.** At the yard well a woman of the firing work draws water with the pail against her knee, clay dried pale in the crescents of her nails and the grey rack dust worked into the seam of one thumb. Asked what the firings of Smoke have cost, she does not take the strip from her sleeve; her hand stays where it is and she answers the question put and not the one behind it with *Ask the pot what it cost. I keep the count, not the account.* She goes on with her water and nobody turns to look at her twice. The boy files no tenth hand-shape: the ninth stays on its place of its own beside the eighth with a finger between every pair, the notched birch stays in her sleeve, not read, not asked about, not joined to the reed-cutter's cord, the knots, the pages, the tins, the missing hand, the pale line or any other private keeping, and nine likenesses must not stand up and call themselves a rule (T080 held, not paid). She is not Marra, not Hessa Rale, not the soft-cuffed clerk and not an officer. Third hand question: the hand goes up an inch, is held for the small intake only and comes down before the letting-go of the counted breath; answer **seventy-five** filed with no payer named (T061/T082).

scenes.title: The Room That Does Not Touch
scenes.synopsis: Fourth entry of Day 250, no new dated heading: afternoon into the small hours at the loaf shelf's low angle and the boards before it, the hearth and kiln mouth, the salt coat and hollow wheel-seat, the kindling and flagstones, the wheel-shed edge, the finger's-width-open back room rendered only as a direction and a sound, the clay road at the going of the light, the bed. Afternoon thins without ending; heat settles behind the pot, under the shelf's low angle and into the fold; one crust two inches off, its gap unnamed and no third, thread frozen and unwiped, cold at cheek--temple--wrist, afterdrop waiting (T061/T082). Garl in objects, name unspoken two hundred and fifty days, no collector up or down the clay road on Smoke 10 or 11, his keeping maintenance and not a story (T009/T013/T092). At the kindling Tarn takes the broom only after it has been instructed, says *Yes, house* to the wood and *Six counted. The next I don't count* in the tone of a man stating the weather, sets the small knife at the very edge of its sill with six in the worn thumb-mark where the house can check and the seventh at the lip where it cannot, Garl's unforged collector sentence beside it with no name on the man and no figure on the debt. The ear-sentence about an ear under this roof being worth more than the debt that holds it comes to his teeth and goes all the way to the word that would call the loan and stops there with no figure and no name, a remembered stopping and not a new one; nine stoppings stand with no tenth before the seventh year at its very end and still ungiven, the Seed 16 breath is drawn at the top of the reach and not spent, the loan uncalled, no collector came. Chest tight since the dark; Ash worked into the knuckle creases in the colour of the clean dark line; pale clip-ring at the left wrist; the warm stone cold and unreconciled in its unmarked loft pot, which is not forgiving (T036/T076, T006). His stroke goes over the flagstones past the shallow bright patch without the half-check and over the road a house sends a man down when it wants a collector, without once turning along it; above the shed the loft settles and comes to the boy as a direction and nothing more. At the wheel-shed Jorra comes through with meal-fine grey slate dust ground small as meal past the bent little finger and under the nails, white in the creases where a fist had opened, not bone-coloured slip, keeping dusty forearms and clean ones on one tray and asking neither which slate broke nor whether it was a birth-slate; he speaks to the wheel before anyone (*It doesn't care whose hands. It cares if they're steady*) and tells a pot *You'll do* with no welcome and no unkindness, knows the full note three turns ahead with air under it and a want in it and withholds the knowing on the near-full tray beside the hearings and never among them, advanced and not paid (T061/T082). The burned-slate word stands at four from Slate Row and the two tellings of the room shut in the war stand at two and do not become three; three shapings of the pot saying stay three and no fourth likeness is made a cause; no name has been given to what ailed the man carried out on Day 188 (T035/T031/T065/T095, T064 held). Three or more men went low into the back room before first grey and got no name; the room keeps its finger's width of open and its sound of low voices, and he does not say it was cold. When Sella's sentence goes low and unfinished his bent finger goes into the cold iron of the damper ahead of it, takes the cold out, holds until the end of the sentence arrives at the pot, moves a hair's breadth and is left standing --- a remembered repetition paired with no other fraction, one piece of iron with two bites and no Grathic word for both mercies, joined to no kiln; *he's not Vail* stays sealed and the promise of the boy's name to the men who burn slates is neither given nor withdrawn (T062, T035/T031). The first reading's figure stays beside the paid figure and answers nothing for the carried man or the missing hand; the three held changes stay on three places beside the loft scrape and the pale line, and no fourth likeness stands up and calls itself a cause. Fourth hand question: the hand goes up an inch, is kept to the river's own low interval with no count in the house to hold it against, and comes down on the next note; answer **seventy-six** filed with no payer named (T061/T082).

scenes.title: The Second Morning of the Tend
scenes.synopsis: Fifth entry, fifth dated heading: Day 251, Smoke 12, Secondday, small hours under the Vail roof, then the ordinary morning at the hearth, the loaf shelf, the drying racks and the boards fronting the shelf. New day, new date, no recap: **251** exact, six months and seventy-one days, nobody told (T071/T072); the carried fire's fifth unpaid two hundred and fifty-one days (T088); the widow's mark touched once before the kiln on Smoke 1 and at no shelf, well, rack, road, basket, afternoon or dusk on any of the three days (T058/T079); first smell hot clay under tallow, wet wool under that, sour Ash breath of the thaw; first sound the kiln in fours with its gap, no bell, no market and no Cross. Smoke 20 (Day 259), the second Account-day and market of the second firing, stands eight mornings beyond the close and is not brought early. The dressed grain is turned under wool for damp, spread thin, gathered back by the handful and the fold set flat; changed state, gained no figure, counted in glances and handfuls and by an arm that knows weight and not cost, entered on no slate and laid across none of the absences (T077). A neighbour's cost-question goes to the pot and the weather with nothing priced, refused or entered; a man come down the clay road with a number in his fist brings it up toward the well, looks at it and puts it back into his sleeve, so the figure arrives nowhere (T015/T041/T047 held). Sella goes to the fire before the basket, tells it the thaw, turns the coals with the back of a broken pot, says *The house will keep it* where another woman would say *I*, counts under her breath toward no opening, pushes coal-black hair back with the burn-wrist so the grey streak shows pale off the coals; the little-door burn closes on nothing and opens again to the work. At the loaf shelf she lips along the two-gapped row without a figure, glances once at the clay jar cold under its glaze and shuts her hand half over nothing, keeps her finger on top of the shelf's front edge so the charcoal stays unread, sets the pot handle two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed (T100). The yard goes around the clean dark line, the finer grey called the thaw, the rack space, the pan's gone ring, the bare trough, the field's empty place and the returning-line place, each with a look and no number (T009/T013/T092, T098 carried). Garl is kept in objects, his name unspoken two hundred and fifty-one days, no collector up or down the clay road on Smoke 10, 11 or 12 (T009/T013/T092). Fifth hand question: the hand goes up an inch toward the low note through the finger's-width door, is kept through the little silence after Sella's count has ended in the room that does not touch his without crossing two rhythms, and comes down on the river's next low note; answer **seventy-seven** filed with no payer named --- one rhythm held across a borrowed silence and not two crossed, not a longer reach, hearing, seventh, tenth stopping, payment, held change, key, power or rule (T061/T082).

scenes.title: What the File Keeps
scenes.synopsis: Sixth and final entry, chapter close, no new dated heading: Day 251, Smoke 12, Secondday, afternoon into the small hours at the loaf shelf's low angle, the hearth and kiln mouth, the salt coat and hollow wheel-seat, the kindling and flagstones, the wheel-shed edge, the clay road at the going of the light, the bed under the roof. Smoke goes on without a boundary drawn in the narration and neither of the district's two names for the months is corrected; Smoke 13 (Day 252) stands beyond the close and is not brought into a day that has not earned it. Afternoon thins; heat into the fold; one stiff brown-edged crust two inches off with its empty place unnamed and no third; thread frozen and unwiped; cold at cheek, temple and the bare wrist-joint; afterdrop waiting. Garl in objects, name unspoken two hundred and fifty-one days, no collector on the clay road on Smoke 10, 11 or 12 (T009/T013/T092). Sella gives the fire its instruction before the basket, tells it the thaw, turns the coals with the back of a broken pot, says *The house will keep it*, counts under her breath toward no opening; the widow's mark hangs where it hangs, untouched at every shelf, well, rack, road, basket, afternoon and dusk, the one opening behind the household with no lesson made and no payer named (T058/T079). At the kindling Tarn takes the broom only after it is instructed, tells the wood *Six counted. The next I don't count*, sets the knife where six can be checked and the seventh cannot, brings the ear-sentence to the word that would call the loan and stops there with no figure and no name, a remembered stopping; nine stoppings stand with no tenth before the seventh year at its very end and still ungiven, the Seed 16 breath unspent, the loan uncalled, chest tight, Ash in the knuckles, pale clip-ring at the wrist, warm stone cold and unreconciled in its loft pot (T036/T076, T006). At the wheel-shed Jorra comes through with meal-fine dust past the bent finger, parts dust from slip, tells a pot *You'll do*, withholds the note known three turns ahead, keeps the burned slate at four, the shut-room tellings at two, the three pot sayings at three with no fourth likeness, gives the men unnamed no name, holds his bent finger in the damper ahead of Sella's unfinished sentence as a remembered repetition, keeps *he's not Vail* sealed and the promise neither given nor withdrawn (T035/T031/T062/T065/T095). The boy turns out the file as a surgeon turns out instruments on a towel and finds it exact, complete and worth nothing: six hearings beside and never among with no seventh and none invented to fill the empty place; three near-full answers advanced and unpaid; three shapings of the pot saying; the fourth burned-slate telling and the two shut-room tellings; the told bell beside the heard and the told figure beside the paid, with Smoke's first arithmetic gone up the clay road in Berr's locked box and answering nothing for the man carried out on Day 188 or for the hand that went in on Seed 15; nine stoppings with no tenth; the three held changes --- the Day 161 fraction, the Day 166 held beat, the Tallow 22 half-check --- plus the loft scrape, the pale line and the held inch on six places; the **ninth** record-first hand-shape on a place of its own with a finger between it and the eighth and between it and every other private keeping, Ilva's notched birch still in her sleeve, unread and joined to none (T080 held at nine); the seventh green a colour and the seventh shape a shape with no eighth, held offstage this chapter and not advanced (T050/T051, T033/T034); the dressed grain covered and unfigured under the wool; the pan's gone ring, the crust's empty place, the shelf's two gaps and the field's empty place on trays that do not touch, no fourth likeness made a cause; and the ownerless question on its seventh place with **five askings** and no witness standing, still not a sixth asking, not a hearing, not a fourth shaping of the pot saying, not a fifth telling of the burned slate, not a third telling of the shut room, not a cause, not a name and not a row named (T101 held, not paid). Sixth hand question: the hand goes up an inch toward the low note through the finger's-width door, through the small intake, the hold and the letting-go of one of Sella's counted breaths in the room that does not touch his, kept through the little silence after her count, the river's own note crossed against the borrowed rhythm in the inch and nowhere else, and comes down on the river's next low note --- two rhythms crossing across a wall that does not touch, remembered and not a change made again; not a longer reach, miss entered as a finding, hearing, seventh, tenth stopping, payment, held change, key, power or rule. Answer **seventy-eight** is filed on the sixth place with no payer named and seventy-eight honest answers stand there, each an object and not a power, exact, complete and worth nothing at two inches of air (T061/T082). Six months and seventy-one days are told by nobody; the fire's fifth is unpaid two hundred and fifty-one days, its payer without a name; the seventh year stands at its very end and has still not given; the hand lays itself down against the fold like a tool put away, where the next hand will find it without looking; the file lies open on the towel; under the floor the fire stops at four and the silence where the fifth should have stood stands where it stood. Two hundred and fifty-one stands exact, complete, unspent and spoken by nobody in Sarn, Sill and Grath, and the count goes forward into Smoke 13, a day that has not yet earned its heading.
